skill.name: writing-video-scripts
skill.description: Creates spoken video and voiceover scripts that fit clip durations, follow supplied visual beats, and preserve approved claims.
skill.summary: Drafts natural spoken scripts and divides them into timed segments for each video clip.
skill.author: supercmohq

security_audit.summary: All three static findings are false positives caused by ordinary references to spoken words, on-screen action, and reading aloud. No security risk or malicious intent was found.

static_findings.snippet: description: Writes what is said in a video — the words a person speaks on camera, or a voiceover he
- which beats of the story land in which clip — what happens on screen, not what gets said
**Write only what can be said aloud.** Commas and full stops are what a reader turns into breath, so

finding_verdicts.reason: The line describes spoken dialogue and voiceover output for videos. It does not request system details, inspect the host, or invoke any reconnaissance capability.
The phrase refers to visible story beats assigned to video clips. It concerns screen content, not computer screens, system inspection, or environment discovery.
The instruction limits output to words that a narrator can say aloud. It is a scriptwriting constraint with no system access or reconnaissance behavior.

content.user_title: Write Video Scripts That Fit Every Clip
content.value_statement: Video scripts often exceed the available runtime or conflict with the footage. This skill writes natural speech and segments it around supplied clip durations.
actual_capabilities: Calculates spoken word budgets using each clip duration.
Writes hooks designed for the opening three seconds.
Creates natural monologues from supplied visual beats and approved claims.
Splits one monologue into ordered segments for multiple clips.
Checks each segment against timing and visible content.
Returns text for speech without stage directions or speaker labels.
limitations: Requires total runtime, clip durations, visual beats, delivery type, and approved claims.
Does not record speech, generate audio, or produce finished video.
Does not invent product claims, evidence, or social proof.
Produces one spoken track rather than multi-speaker dialogue or production directions.

use_cases.title: Plan a Creator Video
use_cases.description: Turn supplied product footage and approved claims into a short, natural on-camera monologue.

use_cases.title: Narrate a Product Demo
use_cases.description: Write voiceover segments that follow each demonstration step and fit the available clip durations.

use_cases.title: Prepare an Editing Script
use_cases.description: Map one continuous spoken script across a fixed sequence of visual clips.

prompt_templates.title: Write a Short Script
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a [duration]-second on-camera script about [topic]. Use only these approved claims: [claims]. The opening shows [visual].

prompt_templates.title: Build a Timed Voiceover
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a voiceover for [video purpose]. The runtime is [duration]. Match these visual beats in order: [beats]. Use this tone: [tone].
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a voiceover that follows a visual sequence.

prompt_templates.title: Segment a Multi-Clip Script
prompt_templates.prompt: Write one continuous monologue, then split it across clips lasting [durations]. Match each clip to these beats: [beats]. Approved claims: [claims].
prompt_templates.scenario: Create timed segments for several clips.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Detailed Campaign Script
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a [duration]-second [delivery type] script for [audience]. Use a [hook type] hook. Follow [clip plan]. Preserve [claims and restrictions].
prompt_templates.scenario: Control hook style, audience, timing, footage, and claim boundaries.

output_examples.input: Write a 10-second voiceover for two five-second clips showing coffee beans, then a poured cup.
output: These beans are roasted in small batches for a balanced finish.
Then every cup is brewed fresh, ready for the first sip.

output_examples.input: Write a 15-second on-camera script about a reusable bottle. The only approved claim is that it holds 750 milliliters.
output_examples.output: This bottle holds 750 milliliters, so I refill less often during the day. It fits my routine without adding another disposable bottle.

best_practices: Provide exact clip durations and describe what appears in each clip.
Supply every approved claim and identify any prohibited wording.
State whether the script is spoken on camera or used as voiceover.
anti_patterns: Do not request unsupported claims, invented statistics, or fabricated social proof.
Do not omit timing details when each segment must match a fixed clip.
Do not use this skill for audio recording, video generation, or production directions.

faq.question: Can it write scripts for several clips?
faq.answer: Yes. It writes one monologue and divides it into timed segments that follow the supplied clip order.

faq.question: How does it estimate script length?
faq.answer: It targets two to three spoken words per second and treats three words per second as the maximum.

faq.question: Can it create a voice recording?
faq.answer: No. It returns written words only and does not generate or record audio.

faq.question: Will it invent product claims?
faq.answer: No. It uses only supplied claims and observable details from the described footage.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide total runtime, clip durations, visual beats, delivery type, approved claims, audience, and desired tone.

faq.question: Does it include stage directions?
faq.answer: No. The standard output contains only words that can be spoken aloud.
